decisions.reason: Selecting a press-and-dispense operator control does not change the required mixing quality, foam, whisk, or high-speed mixing behavior.
The candidate already has a message-143 Event capturing the two press-to-dispense controls and their panel placement.
The cursive K requirement for each dispense button is already fully represented by the candidate's message-143 Event.
The press-and-dispense control decision does not change the spout's geometry, mounting location, orientation, material, or appearance.

The client asks whether the spouts will be removable and notes the cleaning benefit, but the wording does not unambiguously narrow the existing removable-or-flush cleaning requirement to mandatory removability.
Neither the dispense-button choice nor the removability question changes the existing leak-free sealing requirement.
The centered master-power location is already represented by the message-142 Event using message 143 as acceptance context.
The dispense-button decision does not change the platform configuration, cup clearance, height, supported cup size, or footprint.
The source does not alter the requirement to prevent liquid from reaching electrical components.
The operator-control selection does not change splash limits or acceptable splash-mitigation methods.
The source concerns dispense controls and button markings, not the machine placard's text, placement, or viewing orientation.
Choosing functional press-and-dispense buttons does not modify the broader DJ-turntable visual theme.
